subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What memory lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for review, edit, forget/tombstone, supersede, and conflict resolution across the active memory plugin slot?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the correct solution depends on durable storage, plugin API, privacy, rollback, operator UX, and migration choices that automation should not choose independently.

options.title: Define Lifecycle Contract First
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle storage/provenance/status/API semantics, then split implementation into schema, write-path, operator-surface, and UI/CLI PRs.

options.title: Land A Narrow Memory Audit Slice
options.body: Use the draft Memory Audit PR as a partial review-queue path, while leaving edit/forget/conflict semantics tracked here until the contract is settled.

options.title: Defer Broad Lifecycle Work
options.body: Keep current search/promotion/dreaming behavior and handle concrete stale-memory symptoms in narrower issues until memory lifecycle becomes a priority.

recommendation.title: Define Lifecycle Contract First
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle storage/provenance/status/API semantics, then split implementation into schema, write-path, operator-surface, and UI/CLI PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage and event-journal work makes this the strongest available routing signal for the lifecycle storage/provenance decision.
